stages.name: The first week
stages.headline: Survival week. Feed, nappy, sleep, repeat, and nobody knows what day it is.
whatsHappening: Sleep: 14 to 17 hours a day in 2 to 3 hour chunks, and 8 to 12 wakes around the clock.
Feeds: 8 to 12 a day, every 2 to 3 hours, roughly 20 to 40 minutes, day and night alike.
Tummy time: 1 or 2 minutes, a few times a day. Lying on your bare chest counts.
Nights look exactly like days to them. Your job is to make yours different: dim, quiet, no chat.
Weight dips by up to 10 per cent, then climbs back to birth weight by about 2 weeks.
They grip, root, startle, focus about 20 to 30cm away, and already know your voice and smell.

checklist.text: Get the car seat checked by a fitting station before the drive home
checklist.detail: Rear facing, correct recline, straps flat and firm. Most councils and some baby shops have an authorised fitter.

checklist.text: Set the cot up to Red Nose rules before the first night
checklist.detail: Firm flat mattress, no pillows, bumpers, toys or loose bedding. On the back, feet to the bottom end, face uncovered.

checklist.text: Check attachment at every feed: chin in, nose free, wide mouth
checklist.detail: Toe curling pain means a shallow latch. Unlatch and start again. If it still hurts, ring the ABA helpline, that is what it is for.

checklist.text: Change the nappy at every feed, and straight away after a poo
checklist.detail: Barrier cream at every change, girls wipe front to back, and keep a hand on them the whole time.

checklist.text: Burp after every feed, upright on your shoulder for 5 minutes
checklist.detail: No burp after 5 minutes is fine, put them down anyway. Not every feed makes wind.

checklist.text: Tummy time, 2 or 3 minutes after each nappy change
checklist.detail: Always awake and always watched. Your chest or your lap counts just as much as the floor.

checklist.text: Wrap for sleep, firm across the chest but loose around the hips
checklist.detail: Red Nose: light cotton or muslin, arms in, hips and legs free to bend up and out. Never over the face.

checklist.text: Keep the cord stump dry and the nappy folded below it
checklist.detail: It drops off between day 5 and day 15. Redness spreading onto the belly, pus or a smell means ring the nurse today.

checklist.text: Top and tail every day, and skip the full bath this week
checklist.detail: Warm water, cotton wool or a soft cloth, no soap. Face, hands, neck folds, then the bottom last.

checklist.text: Start a feed, sleep and nappy log on paper or in your phone
checklist.detail: Time, which side or how many mL, and every wet and dirty nappy. Expect 5 or 6 heavy wet nappies a day by day 5.

checklist.text: Register the birth, and enrol the baby in Medicare
checklist.detail: Registration is free and due within 60 days at your state or territory registry. The hospital gives you both forms, or use myGov.

checklist.text: Hand the baby to someone else and have a shower
checklist.detail: Twenty minutes is not neglect. If nobody is around, the bassinet or bouncer on the bathroom floor is fine.

appointments.what: Midwife or MCH nurse home visit
appointments.when: Day 1 to 5 after you get home
appointments.note: They weigh the baby, check feeding and the cord, and check on you. Have your feed and nappy log handy.

appointments.what: Newborn screening and hearing check
appointments.when: Before you leave hospital, or in the first few days
appointments.note: The heel prick blood spot test and a hearing screen. Ask for the results if nobody mentions them.

appointments.what: Birth point on the National Immunisation Program
appointments.when: At birth, usually in hospital before you go home
appointments.note: Offered in the first hours or days and recorded on the immunisation register. Ask your midwife if it was missed.

appointments.what: Book the first Maternal and Child Health centre visit
appointments.note: Called MCH in Victoria, child and family health in other states. The home visit nurse usually books it with you.

stages.comingNext: Weeks 2 to 6: still no rhythm, but feeding settles, crying climbs toward its 6 week peak, and the first real smile is close.

stages.name: Settling in
stages.headline: Weeks 2 to 6. No routine yet, more crying than you expected, and a first smile.
whatsHappening: Sleep: still 14 to 17 hours a day, but the longest stretch grows to 3 or 4 hours by week 6.
Feeds: 8 to 12 a day, 20 to 40 minutes, plus an evening cluster that can run for hours.
Tummy time: 3 to 5 minutes after each nappy change, building toward 10 to 15 minutes a day.
Nights: feed, change only if soiled, straight back down. Dim light, no games, no conversation.
Crying peaks around week 6, usually late afternoon and evening. It is normal and it does pass.
New: they hold your gaze, lift their head briefly on their tummy, and smile for real near week 6.

checklist.text: Go to the 2 week MCH visit, and book the 4 and 8 week ones
checklist.detail: Take the baby health record book every time. Write your questions in your phone the night before, you will forget them.

checklist.text: Book your own 6 week postnatal check with the GP now
checklist.detail: It is for the mother: healing, bleeding, mood, contraception, pelvic floor. Book the baby's 6 week check in the same trip.

checklist.text: Book the 6 to 8 week immunisation appointment
checklist.detail: GP or council clinic, free on the National Immunisation Program. Book early, the slots fill up.

checklist.text: Lodge the Centrelink claim for Parental Leave Pay and family payments
checklist.detail: One claim in myGov covers Parental Leave Pay, Family Tax Benefit and the newborn payments. Claim within 52 weeks of the birth.

checklist.text: Give the first proper bath once the cord stump has come away
checklist.detail: Twice a week is plenty. Elbow test the water, 5cm deep, towel open before you start, and never let go or step away.

checklist.text: If you are bottle feeding, sterilise and make bottles one at a time
checklist.detail: Boiled water cooled, powder measured level, never the other way round. Sterilise everything until 12 months.

checklist.text: Express one feed so somebody else can do a bottle
checklist.detail: Label it with the date. Fridge up to 3 days, freezer longer. One bottle given by someone else is one block of sleep for you.

checklist.text: Use the same settling steps every time: wrap, hold, shush, pat, down
checklist.detail: Same order, every sleep, both of you. They learn the sequence long before they learn to self settle.

checklist.text: Dress for the room, and check the back of the neck, not the hands
checklist.detail: Cool hands and feet are normal. Aim for a room you would sleep in comfortably, no hats indoors, no electric blankets.

checklist.text: Take a photo every week, same spot, same day
checklist.detail: Same chair, same blanket, Sunday morning. In six months it will be your only honest record of how fast this went.

checklist.text: Hand the baby over and have a shower, every single day
checklist.detail: Then eat something that is not toast. Swap who gets the first shower, so it does not quietly become one person's job.

checklist.text: Agree now what you both do when the crying will not stop
checklist.detail: Swap every 10 minutes. If you are past it, put them safely in the cot and step outside. Then ring the MCH nurse. Never shake a baby.

appointments.what: MCH nurse centre visits
appointments.when: At about 2 weeks, 4 weeks and 8 weeks
appointments.note: Weight, length, head measurement, feeding and development. Victoria calls these Key Ages and Stages, other states use their own names.

appointments.what: Your 6 week postnatal check
appointments.when: Between 6 and 8 weeks after the birth
appointments.note: With your GP or obstetrician. Bleeding, healing, pain, mood, contraception and pelvic floor. Go even if you feel fine.

appointments.what: Baby's 6 week health check
appointments.note: The GP checks hips, eyes, heart, head growth and weight. Often booked alongside the immunisation visit.

appointments.what: 6 to 8 week point on the National Immunisation Program
appointments.note: The first scheduled visit after the birth point. Free. Expect a grumpy, sleepy baby for a day afterwards.

appointments.what: Mood check for both of you
appointments.when: At the MCH visits and your 6 week check
appointments.note: They ask a short set of questions. Answer them honestly, not bravely. PANDA is on 1300 726 306 if you want to talk sooner.

stages.comingNext: Weeks 6 to 12: the crying eases off, feeds get faster, and the longest sleep of the day moves to the start of the night.

stages.name: Six to twelve weeks
stages.headline: The fog lifts a little. Smiles, longer nights, and feeds that take half the time.
whatsHappening: Sleep: 14 to 16 hours a day. The longest stretch grows to 4 to 6 hours, with about 2 night wakes.
Naps settle to 3 or 4 a day, and the body clock kicks in, so dark nights and bright days start to help.
Feeds: 6 to 8 a day, 15 to 30 minutes. Bottles land around 120 to 150mL, 5 or 6 times a day.
Tummy time: 10 to 15 minutes a day in 3 to 5 minute goes. They push up on their forearms now.
Nights: the longest sleep moves to the front of the night, so an earlier bedtime starts to pay off.
New: real social smiles, cooing, hands to the mouth, steadier head, and eyes tracking you across a room.

checklist.text: Run every night feed the same boring way
checklist.detail: Dim light, no talking, feed, burp, change only if soiled, straight back to the cot. Save the chatting for daytime feeds.

checklist.text: Get the 6 to 8 week immunisation done if it has not happened
checklist.detail: Free on the National Immunisation Program. Check it appears on the immunisation register afterwards.

checklist.text: Go to the 8 week MCH visit, and book the 4 month one
checklist.detail: Weight, length, head, feeding, and a hearing and vision chat. Ask about anything that has worried you at 3am.

checklist.text: Pick a bedtime between 6.30 and 8pm and start the same wind down
checklist.detail: Wash or bath, feed, wrap, dark quiet room, same order every night. It is a signal, not a schedule, so late nights will not ruin it.

checklist.text: Get outside with them in daylight once a day
checklist.detail: Morning light helps the body clock settle. It also gets you out of the house, which honestly matters more right now.

checklist.text: Keep wrapping, but watch for the first sign of rolling
checklist.detail: Red Nose: the moment they show any sign of rolling, stop wrapping the arms in and move to a safe infant sleeping bag.

checklist.text: Build tummy time to 10 to 15 minutes a day, broken up
checklist.detail: Roll a towel under the chest if they hate it, and get down on the floor at their eye level. They do it for your face, not the mat.

checklist.text: Re-check the cot against Red Nose: firm, flat, nothing loose
checklist.detail: No pillows, doonas, bumpers, positioners or toys. On the back every sleep, in a sleeping bag or a firmly tucked sheet.

checklist.text: Try putting them down drowsy rather than fully asleep
checklist.detail: Some nights it works and some nights it does not. Both are completely fine at this age, so do not turn it into a project.

checklist.text: Split the night into two shifts so each of you gets one long block
checklist.detail: One of you is on until 2am, the other after. An expressed bottle makes it possible. Four unbroken hours changes everything.

checklist.text: Taper the log down to feeds and the overnight pattern
checklist.detail: You do not need to write down everything any more. Keep enough to answer the nurse and to spot a real change.

checklist.text: If you skipped your own 6 week check, go this week
checklist.detail: Mood, bleeding, pain, pelvic floor, contraception. Three months of broken sleep is not a reason to put yourself last.

appointments.what: 6 to 8 week point on the National Immunisation Program
appointments.note: Free. If you are past 8 weeks it is not too late, ring the clinic and catch it up.

appointments.what: MCH nurse visit
appointments.note: Growth measurements, feeding, development, hearing and vision questions, and a mood check for both parents.

appointments.what: Your 6 week postnatal check, if not done
appointments.note: GP or obstetrician. Worth going late rather than not at all.

appointments.what: 4 month point on the National Immunisation Program
appointments.note: The next scheduled visit. Book it now rather than waiting for a reminder letter, and book the 4 month MCH visit too.

stages.comingNext: Three to six months: rolling, laughing, longer nights, a sleep wobble around 4 months, and solids on the horizon at 6 months.

stages.name: Three to six months
stages.headline: Rolling, laughing, grabbing. Sleep gets better, then wobbles at 4 months.
whatsHappening: Sleep: 12 to 15 hours a day, with 9 to 11 hours overnight and 1 or 2 wakes on a typical night.
Naps drop from 4 to about 3, then 2 by six months, each 30 minutes to 2 hours long.
Feeds: 5 or 6 milk feeds a day, 15 to 25 minutes. Milk only until around 6 months.
Tummy time: 20 to 30 minutes a day spread out. Rolling usually turns up between 4 and 6 months.
Nights: expect a wobble around 16 to 18 weeks when sleep gets lighter. That is development, not a setback.
New: rolls over, grabs and mouths everything, laughs out loud, babbles, steady head, sits propped up.

checklist.text: Stop wrapping the arms the day you see any sign of rolling
checklist.detail: Red Nose rule, no exceptions and no waiting for a full roll. Move to a safe sleeping bag with armholes and a fitted neck.

checklist.text: Clear the cot again now they can roll and shuffle
checklist.detail: Nothing loose, no bumpers, no toys, no positioners. Always start them on the back, then let them find their own position.

checklist.text: Get the 4 month immunisation done
checklist.detail: Free on the National Immunisation Program. Book the 6 month one before you leave the clinic, while you are already there.

checklist.text: Go to the 4 month MCH visit
checklist.detail: Growth, rolling, hearing, vision and feeding. Bring the list of questions you have been meaning to ask since week 3.

checklist.text: Put them on a rug on the floor instead of a bouncer or seat
checklist.detail: Twenty minutes of free floor time beats any toy. Rolling, reaching and pushing up all have to happen down there.

checklist.text: Roll proof the room: nothing in reach, no cords, no gaps
checklist.detail: Change them on the floor rather than a change table once they can roll. It only takes one second of looking away.

checklist.text: When sleep goes backwards at 4 months, change nothing for two weeks
checklist.detail: Same wind down, same cot, same boring nights. It settles. Starting a brand new method mid wobble usually drags it out.

checklist.text: If they feed twice a night, try keeping the second one short
checklist.detail: Same dim, silent routine. Plenty of babies drop a night feed on their own somewhere in here, so do not push it.

checklist.text: Watch for the three solids signs, around but not before 6 months
checklist.detail: Head steady and sits with support, reaches for your food, opens the mouth for a spoon. Around 6 months, never before 4.

checklist.text: Buy the solids kit before you need it: high chair, bibs, soft spoons
checklist.detail: A high chair that straps in and wipes clean. Check it carries the Australian standard label, and that the feet are supported.

checklist.text: Have a teething plan ready: cold teether, clean finger, extra bibs
checklist.detail: Drool, chewing and one red cheek are normal. A fever, a rash or refused feeds is not teething, so ring the nurse instead.

checklist.text: Book one evening where somebody else does the bedtime
checklist.detail: An hour out of the house with your phone on. You are also a couple, and that part has been on hold since April.

appointments.what: 4 month point on the National Immunisation Program
appointments.note: Free. Grumpy, sleepy and off their feeds for a day afterwards is expected. Extra cuddles and feeds on demand.

appointments.what: MCH nurse visit
appointments.note: Weight, length, head, rolling and head control, plus hearing and vision questions. Book the next visit before you leave.

appointments.what: 6 month point on the National Immunisation Program
appointments.note: The next scheduled visit, free. Ask at the 4 month appointment what else is recommended for their age.

appointments.what: GP visit for feeding or growth worries
appointments.when: Any time between the scheduled visits
appointments.note: Slow weight gain, reflux that stops feeds, or a baby who is not rolling by 6 months is worth a proper look.

stages.comingNext: Six to nine months: sitting alone, first foods, two solid naps, and a baby who crosses the room the moment you blink.

stages.name: Six to nine months
stages.headline: First foods, sitting up, and a baby who is suddenly mobile.
whatsHappening: Sleep: 11 to 14 hours a day. About 10 to 11 overnight, with 0 or 1 wakes on a good night.
Naps settle to 2 a day, 1 to 2 hours each, usually mid morning and early afternoon.
Feeds: milk is still the main event at 4 or 5 feeds, plus solids going from 1 meal to 3 by 9 months.
Tummy time becomes floor time: 30 to 60 minutes a day of rolling, sitting, crawling and reaching.
Nights: around 8 months they wake because they miss you, not because they are hungry. Short, dim, boring reassurance.
New: sits unaided, crawls or commandos, first teeth, picks things up, turns to their name, babbles ba-ba and da-da.

checklist.text: Start solids with iron rich food once a day, after a milk feed
checklist.detail: Iron fortified cereal, pureed meat, lentils or tofu. Smooth first, then lumpier within a few weeks. Milk still comes first.

checklist.text: Introduce the common allergy foods one at a time, before 12 months
checklist.detail: Egg, peanut, dairy, wheat, fish, sesame, soy and tree nuts, as smooth paste or butter. At home, in the morning. Never whole nuts.

checklist.text: Offer water in an open or free flowing cup with meals
checklist.detail: No juice, no cordial, no sweet drinks, no tea. Cooled boiled water until about 12 months if you want to be careful.

checklist.text: Drop the cot mattress to the lowest setting now they can sit
checklist.detail: Red Nose: nothing in the cot they can climb on or get tangled in, so take out mobiles, cot toys and any hanging cords.

checklist.text: Get the 6 month immunisation done
checklist.detail: Free on the National Immunisation Program. Ask at the same visit what else is recommended for their age.

checklist.text: Go to the 6 or 8 month MCH visit
checklist.detail: Sitting, crawling, hearing, vision, teeth and how solids are going. States run this at slightly different ages, so check yours.

checklist.text: Baby proof at floor level: latches, gates, cords, power points
checklist.detail: Get on your knees and look. Anything that fits inside a toilet roll is a choking risk. Button batteries out of the house entirely.

checklist.text: Eat at the same time, with them strapped into the high chair
checklist.detail: Straps done up, feet supported, never on a bench or table. Mess is how they learn, so put an old sheet underneath.

checklist.text: Settle into 2 naps a day at roughly the same times
checklist.detail: About 2.5 to 3 hours of awake time between sleeps at this age. Watch the baby more than the clock, but keep the order the same.

checklist.text: Agree one script for the 8 month night wakes and both use it
checklist.detail: In, hand on the chest, a few quiet words, out. No lights, no lifting unless you have to. The same every time, from both of you.

checklist.text: Start brushing as soon as the first tooth comes through
checklist.detail: A soft baby brush and plain water, twice a day. No toothpaste yet unless your dentist or MCH nurse tells you otherwise.

checklist.text: Check the car seat still fits: shoulder height markers, not age
checklist.detail: Keep them rear facing for as long as the markers allow. Get it re-checked by a fitter whenever you change the setting.

appointments.what: 6 month point on the National Immunisation Program
appointments.note: Free. Book the 12 month one before you leave, because nothing routine falls due in between to remind you.

appointments.what: MCH nurse visit
appointments.when: At about 6 or 8 months, depending on your state
appointments.note: Growth, sitting and crawling, hearing, vision, teeth and solids. Victoria runs a 6 month and an 8 month visit.

appointments.what: Hearing and development check
appointments.when: At the MCH visit around 8 months
appointments.note: They watch how the baby responds to sound and to their name. Raise it sooner if they never startle or turn to a voice.

appointments.what: 12 month point on the National Immunisation Program
appointments.note: The next scheduled visit after 6 months. Nothing routine is due in between unless your GP says otherwise.

stages.comingNext: Nine to twelve months: pulling up, cruising the furniture, first words, three meals a day, and the 12 month immunisation and check.

stages.name: Nine to twelve months
stages.headline: Pulling up, first words, three meals a day, and a first birthday in sight.
whatsHappening: Sleep: 11 to 14 hours a day. Usually 10 to 12 overnight, and most babies no longer need a night feed.
Naps: 2 a day, sometimes shortening toward 1 longer one near the first birthday.
Feeds: 3 meals and 2 snacks, plus 3 or 4 milk feeds. Finger food at every single meal.
Floor time has replaced tummy time: pulling to stand, cruising the furniture, and crawling at real speed.
Nights: they can stand up in the cot now. Lowest mattress setting, sleeping bag rather than blankets, no bumpers.
New: pulls to stand, cruises, points, waves, says a word or two with meaning, and may take a first step.

checklist.text: Get the 12 month immunisation done
checklist.detail: Free on the National Immunisation Program. Book it near their birthday so it does not quietly slide into month 14.

checklist.text: Go to the 12 month MCH visit
checklist.detail: Growth, walking, words, teeth, eating and your own wellbeing. It is the last routine visit before 18 months.

checklist.text: Book a first dental check by their first birthday
checklist.detail: Or within six months of the first tooth, whichever comes first. Many public dental services see babies at no cost.

checklist.text: Cot base at the lowest setting, nothing they can stand on
checklist.detail: Red Nose: no bumpers, no cot toys, no pillows. A fitted sleeping bag beats blankets once they stand up and move around.

checklist.text: Move daytime milk from a bottle to a cup
checklist.detail: Aim to be off bottles around 12 months. Swap one feed at a time into an open or free flowing cup, starting with the easiest.

checklist.text: Hold off on cow's milk as a drink until 12 months
checklist.detail: Dairy in food is already fine. Full cream cow's milk as a drink from 12 months, and no reduced fat milk before 2 years.

checklist.text: Sit down and eat the same meal together, three times a day
checklist.detail: They copy you, not a spoon. Soft finger food cut long and thin, and never leave them eating on their own.

checklist.text: Do an infant first aid and choking course, both of you
checklist.detail: Three hours on one Saturday and you will never have to wonder again. Book it before they are properly mobile.

checklist.text: If they still feed overnight, shorten it rather than cut it
checklist.detail: Most babies this age wake from habit or teeth, not hunger. Same dim, quiet script, a little shorter each night.

checklist.text: Let them pull up and cruise barefoot on a clear floor
checklist.detail: No shoes needed indoors, bare feet grip better. Clear a loop of steady furniture and move anything that tips or slides.

checklist.text: Name everything out loud, and read the same book every night
checklist.detail: Point, wait, then repeat back whatever sound they make. Twenty minutes of talking to them beats any screen or app.

checklist.text: Pull the weekly photos into one album before the birthday
checklist.detail: Fifty two photos, one a page. It is the best present the two of you will give yourselves this year.

appointments.what: 12 month point on the National Immunisation Program
appointments.note: Free. Check afterwards that it has gone onto the immunisation register, because childcare and some payments rely on it.

appointments.what: MCH nurse visit
appointments.note: Growth, development, eating, teeth, home safety and a mood check for both parents. Bring the health record book.

appointments.what: First dental check
appointments.when: By the first birthday, or 6 months after the first tooth
appointments.note: A quick look, a clean and advice on brushing. Public dental services cover babies in most states.

appointments.what: 18 month immunisation and MCH visit
appointments.note: The next scheduled points after the first birthday. Nothing routine is due between 12 and 18 months.

stages.comingNext: After 12 months: one nap, cow's milk in a cup, walking, and the next immunisation and MCH visit waiting at 18 months.
